mainTopic: The moving courtyard (חצר מהלכת), and acquiring a found item or פאה on behalf of someone else (מגו)
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: riding an animal acquires it in the public domain, and also for an important person, a woman, or a lowly person. Then רבי אלעזר asks whether pulling an animal can acquire the vessels on its back. רבא answers no. Even if the buyer owns the animal, it is a חצר מהלכת, a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard does not acquire. Standing still does not help, and the הלכה is that it works only when the animal is tied up. Challenges from fish jumping into a boat and a גט thrown into a walking woman's basket are answered: the boat and the basket themselves are resting, and something else moves them. A new משנה follows about a rider who asks his friend to hand him a found item. The גמרא brings the argument between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about gathering פאה for a poor person. עולא explains that argument through one or two steps of מגו, and רב נחמן begins to challenge him from our משנה. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four cases where riding the animal does acquire it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion about riding an animal to acquire it. It lists four cases where riding does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is in the public domain, he acquires. If he is an important person, he acquires. If the buyer is a woman, she acquires. If he is a lowly person, he acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the earlier discussion about acquiring an animal by riding it. It lists situations where riding does count as a way to acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding normally works only where people usually ride. In the public domain people commonly ride. An important person or a woman normally rides rather than leading the animal. A lowly person rides anywhere, so for each of these people riding is the normal way to take control of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, a public area
A lowly person, someone who doesn't care about his dignity

steps.whatToRemember: Riding acquires an animal when riding is the normal thing for that place or for that person.

phrases.english: And if it is the public domain, he acquires;
phrases.notes: He means riding the animal there, which is the case discussed just before this.

phrases.english: and if he is an important person, he acquires;
and if she is a woman, she acquires;
and if he is a lowly person, he acquires.
phrases.notes: This is someone who doesn't care how he looks, so he rides even where others wouldn't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (on the previous daf) about acquiring an animal by riding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Riding acquires in the public domain, and also for an important person, a woman, or a lowly person.

steps.title: Can pulling an animal acquire the vessels on it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks about a seller who says, 'Pull this animal in order to acquire the vessels on it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: if someone says to his friend, 'Pull this animal in order to acquire the vessels that are on it,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אלעזר asks whether pulling an animal can serve as the act that acquires the vessels sitting on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משיכה, pulling, is a normal way to acquire an animal. The question is whether that same act can also acquire other objects resting on the animal, even though the buyer never touched them.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raises a question that may stay open)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked:
One who says to his fellow:
"Pull this animal
in order to acquire the vessels that are on it" — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question related to acquiring through an animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does pulling an animal acquire the vessels on top of it?

steps.title: Problem with the wording 'in order to acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'in order to acquire' is not a real instruction to acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In order to acquire'? Did he tell him 'Acquire'?
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא challenges how the question was worded. The words 'in order to acquire' never actually tell the buyer to acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To acquire something from another person, the seller has to clearly give permission, such as by saying 'קני', acquire. Saying only 'in order to acquire' is too weak, so with that wording the buyer would obviously get nothing. That leaves no real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he say to him? (here a challenge: he didn't!)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the answer to רבי אלעזר's question. It only fixes the wording so that the question makes sense.

phrases.english: "In order to acquire"?
Did he say to him "Acquire"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי אלעזר's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'לקנות' in רבי אלעזר's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a clear instruction 'קני', the buyer cannot acquire at all, so the question would be pointless.

steps.title: The corrected question: 'Pull and acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question so the seller clearly says 'acquire.' Now the real issue is whether pulling the animal works for the vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is: 'Pull this animal and acquire the vessels on it.' What is the law? Does pulling the animal work to acquire the vessels, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the question. The seller clearly says 'acquire,' so the only issue left is whether this act works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission is no longer in doubt. What remains is whether the act itself is good enough: can pulling one object, the animal, transfer ownership of other objects, the vessels, that are only riding on it?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it effective? Does it work?
To make someone acquire, to transfer ownership

phrases.english: Rather: "Pull this animal
and acquire the vessels that are on it" — what is the law?
Is pulling the animal effective
to acquire the vessels, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״מְשׁוֹךְ בְּהֵמָה זוֹ וּקְנֵי כֵּלִים שֶׁעָלֶיהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem by restating the question with 'וקני'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question used the weak wording 'לקנות'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about 'pull and acquire', so the only issue is whether pulling the animal works for the vessels.

steps.title: רבא: a moving courtyard does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that it doesn't work. Even if the buyer acquired the animal too, it is a moving courtyard, and that cannot acquire the vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even if he told him 'Acquire the animal and acquire the vessels,' would he acquire the vessels? It is a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי אלעזר's question with a 'no.' He shows that even a stronger case fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person's courtyard (חצר) acquires objects placed in it for him. If the buyer owns the animal, the animal could act like his courtyard for the vessels on it. But an animal walks around, so it is a חצר מהלכת, and a moving courtyard does not acquire. If the vessels are not acquired even when the buyer owns the animal, they are certainly not acquired just by pulling it.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard, a person's property that can acquire items placed in it

steps.whatToRemember: A חצר מהלכת, a moving courtyard such as an animal, does not acquire the items on it. So pulling an animal does not acquire the vessels it carries. Step 7 gives the one exception, when the animal is tied up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule of חצר מהלכת, which matters for any case where items sit on something that moves.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he said to him, "Acquire the animal
and acquire the vessels," does he acquire the vessels?
It is a moving courtyard,
phrases.notes: Once the animal is his, it works like his own courtyard, except that it walks around.

phrases.english: and a moving courtyard does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ קְנֵי בְּהֵמָה וּקְנֵי כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the corrected question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Even if the buyer acquires the animal, the animal is a חצר מהלכת, which does not acquire the vessels on it.

steps.title: Standing still does not help
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers whether the animal could act as a courtyard while it is standing still, and rejects the idea. Whatever cannot acquire while walking also cannot acquire while standing or sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the animal works when it stands still, there is a rule: whatever does not acquire when it walks also does not acquire when it stands or sits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible way out of רבא's answer. Someone might say the animal works as a courtyard while it stands still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a moving animal is a moving courtyard and cannot acquire. One might suggest that a pause in walking would let it work. The גמרא answers with a general rule: something that is a walking type of thing stays in that category even when it is resting at the moment.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible suggestion)

phrases.english: And if you would say: when it stood still,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כֹּל שֶׁאִילּוּ מְהַלֵּךְ לֹא קָנָה –
phrases.english: but isn't it so that anything which, when walking, does not acquire
also does not acquire when standing or sitting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off a possible escape from רבא's ruling in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that a standing animal could act as a courtyard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Something that cannot acquire while walking also cannot acquire while standing or sitting.

steps.title: The הלכה: only when the animal is tied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the animal can acquire the vessels on it only when it is tied up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: when the animal is tied up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final הלכה. The animal can acquire the vessels only if it is tied up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking does not work, and standing still does not work either. Tying the animal changes it into something that truly cannot move. That makes it a fixed courtyard, so it can acquire what is on it.
steps.whatToRemember: An animal acts as a courtyard for the vessels on it only when it is tied up. Walking does not work, and just standing still does not work either.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: when it is tied up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after steps 5 and 6 ruled out walking and standing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A tied-up animal can acquire the vessels on it for its owner.

steps.title: Challenge: fish jumping into a moving boat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenge רבא. Fish jump into a moving boat, and by רבא's logic the owner should not acquire them, which seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רבא: If so, if someone was traveling in a boat and fish jumped in, is the boat also a moving courtyard so that he does not acquire them?
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים attack רבא's rule about a moving courtyard. They bring a case where it seems obvious that the person does acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boat is moving, just like a walking animal. If a moving courtyard cannot acquire, then the boat owner should not get the fish. Everyone assumes he does get them, so רבא's rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces a challenge from a strange result)
Is it really so too? (asks in surprise)

phrases.english: They said to him, Rav Pappa

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rava:
If that is so: if one was traveling in a boat,
and fish jumped and fell into the boat,
would it also be a moving courtyard
and he does not acquire?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's moving-courtyard rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a moving courtyard cannot acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A boat moves too, so by that rule fish landing in it should not be acquired. That result seems unacceptable.

steps.title: The boat itself is resting
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a boat is not a moving courtyard. The boat itself rests, and the water carries it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A boat rests in place, and it is the water that carries it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule by showing that the boat is different from a walking animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal moves by itself, so it is a moving courtyard. A boat does not move on its own. It sits still and the water moves it, so it counts as a resting courtyard and can acquire the fish.

phrases.english: He said to him: A boat rests in place,
and it is the water that carries it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the boat challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the boat is not itself moving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A boat on the move is a moving courtyard like a walking animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boat itself rests and the water moves it, so it can acquire.

steps.title: Challenge: a גט thrown into a walking woman's basket
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי. A woman is walking in the public domain and a גט is thrown into her lap or basket. By the moving-courtyard rule she would not be divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If so, if a woman was walking in the public domain and her husband threw a גט into her lap or her basket, is she here too not divorced?
steps.whatsHappening: Another challenge to the moving-courtyard rule, this time from the laws of גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can receive a גט in her basket because it acts as her courtyard. If she is walking, the basket is moving, so by רבא's rule it should not work. That seems to go against the accepted הלכה that she is divorced.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה הָיְתָה מְהַלֶּכֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: If that is so: if she was walking in the public domain
and he threw her a get into her lap
or into her basket,
here too, is she not divorced?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה הָיְתָה מְהַלֶּכֶת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the moving-courtyard rule, parallel to step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a moving courtyard cannot acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A walking woman's basket moves with her, so by that rule a גט thrown into it should not divorce her. That result seems wrong.

steps.title: The basket rests and she walks under it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the basket itself is resting, and the woman is the one walking beneath it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Her basket rests in place, and it is she who walks beneath it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge the same way the boat challenge was answered: the basket itself is not moving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basket does not move on its own. It sits still on her, and she is the one walking. So it is not a moving courtyard, and the גט works.
steps.whatToRemember: A 'moving courtyard' means something that moves by itself, like a walking animal. A boat carried by water or a basket carried by a woman counts as resting, so it can acquire.

phrases.english: He said to him: Her basket rests in place,
and it is she who walks beneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the גט challenge of step 10, using the same logic as step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the basket is not itself moving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A basket carried by a walking woman is a moving courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket rests and she walks under it, so the גט is acquired and she is divorced.

steps.title: The rider who asks his friend to hand him a found item
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches two cases. In the first, the friend picks up the item, says he acquired it, and keeps it. In the second, he hands it to the rider and only afterward claims he acquired it first; then his claim is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man was riding an animal and saw a lost object. He told his friend, 'Give it to me.' If the friend picked it up and said, 'I acquired it,' then the friend keeps it. But if he first handed it to the rider and only then said, 'I acquired it first,' his words mean nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case about two people and one found item. It asks who owns the item when one person picks it up after the other asked for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the item does not give the rider ownership. Picking it up (lifting) is what acquires. So the friend who lifts it and declares 'I have acquired it' keeps it. Once he has already handed it over, his claim that he acquired it first does not help: even if he did, he then gave it to the rider.

keyTerms.meaning: He has said nothing; his claim has no effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rider owns the item because he saw it first. Seeing does not acquire. Only the lifting counts.

phrases.english: MISHNA
If one was riding on an animal
and saw a found item
and said to his friend: "Give it to me."
If the friend took it and said:
"I have acquired it" — he has acquired it.
If, after he gave it to him, he said:
"I acquired it first"
— he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה וְרָאָה אֶת הַמְּצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the discussion of the moving courtyard, which ended with the boat and the basket cases (steps 8–11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who lifts the found item and declares at once that he acquired it keeps it. A claim made only after handing it over is void.

steps.title: A related משנה: picking up פאה for a poor person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about someone who gathers פאה and says it is for a certain poor person. רבי אליעזר says he acquired it for that poor person. חכמים say it must go to the first poor person he meets.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in another משנה: someone gathered פאה and said, 'This is for so-and-so, the poor man.' רבי אליעזר says he acquired it for that poor man. The חכמים say he must give it to the first poor person he comes across.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by bringing a source from somewhere else about picking something up on behalf of another person. It is setting up a discussion of whether one person can acquire for someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה raises the question of whether the friend who lifted the item acquired it for the rider. This פאה case deals with exactly that idea: can a person's lifting acquire for someone else? רבי אליעזר says yes, and חכמים say no.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
The corner of the field left for the poor
He acquired it on his behalf
The first poor person he encounters

phrases.english: GEMARA
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פאה 4:9.

phrases.english: One who gathered the פאה,
and said: "This is for so-and-so, a poor man,"
Rabbi Eliezer says: He acquired it for him.
And the Sages say:
He should give it to the first poor person he finds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related source to examine the idea of acquiring an object for another person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: gathering פאה for a named poor person acquires it for him. חכמים: it does not, so it goes to the first poor person found.

steps.title: The dispute is only about a rich man gathering for a poor man
steps.stepSummary: עולא, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, says the argument is only where the one gathering the פאה is rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The argument is about a rich man who gathers for a poor man.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows down the case of the dispute. He says the argument is only about a rich person picking up פאה for a poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rich man may not take פאה for himself. So the question becomes whether he can acquire it for someone else when it would not be his to take. This narrowing sets up the explanation of both sides that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A rich person, who may not take פאה
A poor person, who is entitled to פאה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The dispute is from a rich man to a poor man,
phrases.notes: He means a rich man picked up the פאה on behalf of a poor man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case where the פאה dispute applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי אליעזר and חכמים is only where a rich man gathered the פאה for a poor man.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reasoning: two steps of מגו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reasons in two steps. The rich man could give up his property and become poor, so the פאה counts as fit for him. And since he can acquire it for himself, he can also acquire it for his friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: since the rich man could, if he wanted, make his property ownerless, become poor, and be allowed to take פאה, it counts as fit for him even now. And since he can acquire it for himself, he can also acquire it for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אליעזר lets a rich man acquire פאה for a poor man. It does this with two steps of 'since' reasoning, called מגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first מגו: he could become poor, so the פאה is considered fit for him now. The second מגו: since he could acquire it for himself, he can acquire it for someone else. Each step builds on the one before it.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since": because he could do X, we treat him as able to do Y
He acquires on behalf of his friend

steps.confusionAlert: The rich man does not actually give away his property. The point is only that he could, and that possibility is enough for רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Eliezer holds:
since, if he wanted, he could make his property ownerless
and he would be poor, and it would be fit for him —
now too it is fit for him.
And since he can acquire it for himself,
he can also acquire it for his friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אליעזר's side of the dispute that the previous step narrowed to a rich man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר accepts two stacked steps of מגו, so a rich man can acquire פאה for a poor man.

steps.title: The חכמים accept one מגו but not two
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that we may rely on one מגו but not on two stacked together. So the rich man cannot acquire the פאה for the poor man.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים hold: we say one מגו, but we do not say two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side. The חכמים reject רבי אליעזר's chain because it needs two steps of מגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides agree that a מגו is a valid kind of reasoning. They only argue about stacking one on top of another. Since the rich man's case needs two, the חכמים say he does not acquire, and the פאה goes to the first poor person found.

keyTerms.meaning: We say; we accept this reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: In the פאה case, a rich man picking up for a poor man needs two steps of מגו: he could become poor, and he could acquire for himself. רבי אליעזר accepts both steps. The חכמים accept only one מגו, so for them the rich man does not acquire.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
one מגו we say,
two מגו we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's side, in contrast to רבי אליעזר's two-step reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים rely on a single מגו but not on two, so a rich man cannot acquire פאה for a poor man.

steps.title: A poor person gathering for another poor person: everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: עולא completes his statement. When a poor person gathers פאה for another poor person, both רבי אליעזר and the חכמים agree that he acquires it for his friend, because only one מגו is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when a poor person gathers for another poor person, everyone agrees he acquired it for him. Since he can acquire it for himself, he can also acquire it for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes his point. The argument is only about a rich gatherer, but a poor gatherer can definitely acquire פאה for another poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person may take פאה for himself directly, so he does not need the 'he could become poor' step. That leaves only one מגו: since he can acquire for himself, he can acquire for his friend. Even the חכמים accept a single מגו.

keyTerms.meaning: From a poor person to a poor person (a poor gatherer acting for another poor person)
Since he can acquire for himself

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the argument is only about a rich gatherer (two מגו steps). With a poor gatherer there is only one מגו, and everyone agrees he acquires for his friend.

phrases.english: But from a poor person to a poor person,
phrases.notes: He means a poor person who gathers the פאה on behalf of another poor person.

phrases.english: everyone agrees he acquired it for him,
because since he can acquire it for himself,
he can also acquire it for his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מֵעָנִי לְעָנִי, דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל זָכָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's limit from step 14 by stating the case where there is no argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person who gathers פאה for another poor person acquires it for him according to everyone, based on a single מגו.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the argument should apply even between two poor people
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges עולא. He says the argument should also apply when a poor person gathers for a poor person. He brings in the משנה of the rider, since with a found item everyone is like a poor person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to עולא: Let the Master say the argument applies even from a poor person to a poor person. With a found item everyone counts as poor, and we learned in the משנה: if someone was riding an animal, saw a found item, and told his friend 'Give it to me,' and the friend took it and said 'I acquired it,' then he acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on עולא. He claims the argument is even about a poor gatherer, and he points to the משנה of the rider as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone may take a found item, the same way any poor person may take פאה. So the friend picking up the item for the rider is like a poor person gathering for a poor person. The משנה says the friend keeps it, which suggests that picking up an item for someone else does not automatically acquire it for him.

keyTerms.meaning: But let the Master say (a respectful way of suggesting a different position)
Everyone is 'poor' with respect to it (everyone may take it)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is saying that people who find items are actually poor. The point is only that a found item is open to everyone, just as פאה is open to every poor person.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Ulla:
But let the Master say
that from a poor person to a poor person there is an argument,
for with a found item
everyone is like a poor person regarding it,
phrases.notes: Anyone may pick up a found item, just like any poor person may take פאה.

phrases.english: and we learned in the משנה:
If one was riding on an animal
and saw a found item,
and said to his friend, 'Give it to me,'
and the friend took it and said, 'I have acquired it,'
he has acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְעוּלָּא: וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's claim in step 17 that everyone agrees in the case of a poor person gathering for a poor person.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that everyone agrees a poor person can acquire פאה for another poor person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rider case is like poor-for-poor, and the משנה rules that the friend keeps the item. That suggests poor-for-poor is also under dispute.

steps.title: Setting up the proof: if the argument covers two poor people
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן begins to spell out his proof. He starts by assuming the argument applies even between two poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well if you say the argument applies even from a poor person to a poor person...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב נחמן starts explaining why the משנה fits well if the argument covers a poor gatherer too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אי אמרת בשלמא opens an 'it works well this way, but not the other way' argument. Here he states the version that works. The next lines will show which opinion the משנה follows, and why עולא's view creates a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well if you say (opens an argument comparing two possibilities)

phrases.english: It works out well if you say
that from a poor person to a poor person there is an argument,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא: מֵעָנִי לְעָנִי מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's challenge by starting to lay out the logic of his proof from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that everyone agrees in the poor-for-poor case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He begins to show that the משנה fits only if poor-for-poor is under dispute. The rest of the argument comes next.
